summary.overview: Bookshop sells books online. A React web app calls a FastAPI service, which keeps orders in its own PostgreSQL database, searches a catalogue index that the catalogue team runs, and charges cards through an external payment provider.
findings: The card is charged before the order is stored (`api/bookshop/orders/service.py:31-32`): if the insert fails, the reader has paid and no order exists.
The charge is sent without an idempotency key (`api/bookshop/payments/client.py:10`), so a retried request can charge the card twice.
Search goes straight to another team's index (`api/bookshop/search/index.py:13`), with no fallback when it is unavailable.
recommendations: Store the order as pending before charging, then mark it paid; refund when the update fails.
Send an idempotency key with each charge so the request can be retried safely.
